For one whose physical practice is without flaw or leakage, the blessings and merit thereof are beyond comparison.”
“Śubhaprabha!

Suppose a person were to fill the ten directions, reaching as far upward as the twenty-eighth heaven, with the seven treasures and offer them in alms for hundreds of thousands of kalpas without ceasing or resting.
If those four classes of people were to practice and perfect the fourfold dharmas of the merit of the Radiant Samādhi, it would exceed the merit of that gift by hundreds of billions of times.
Why is this so? For merit is subject to exhaustion, suffering, coming and going, toil, and the need for food and drink;

yet practicing this Samādhi of the Perfected Radiance is free from these five things. It is tranquil and pure, wherein all [defilements] are utterly extinguished; this is called the most honored, and is therefore said to be superior.
“Suvimalaprabha!
You should proclaim these precepts so that all may hear, receive, uphold, and practice them; this is what a wise man ought to diligently exhort others to do.
The Buddha said to Suvimalaprabha:

"After my parinirvāṇa, if there be anyone who practices this Samādhi of Perfect Radiance, or who copies, maintains, makes offerings to, or pays homage to its scrolls, they shall be protected by twelve great celestial deities. These shall ensure that they do not suffer injustice or calamity, that they remain secure wherever they are, and that they are not harmed or injured by evil."

I shall now tell you the names of these deities. Should one encounter hardships such as water, fire, bandits, or warfare, if they skillfully recite and practice the text of this sutra and do not abandon it because of resentment or distress, these twelve celestial deities will immediately go to protect them and shall never allow calamities to befall them unexpectedly.
The Buddha’s word is not twofold; you should proclaim it widely to all people and cause them to recite and practice it:
“There is a deity named Mahāpāla; furthermore, there is a deity named Puṇyatrāta;
furthermore, there is a deity named Gaṇarakṣa; furthermore, there is a deity named Anābādha.”
Furthermore, there is a deity named Good Leader; furthermore, there is a deity named Radiance;
furthermore, there is a deity named Path-Virtue; furthermore, there is a deity named Extractor of Suffering.
Furthermore, there is a deity named Great Deliverance; furthermore, there is a deity named Deliverance from Calamity;
furthermore, there is a deity named Tranquility; furthermore, there is a deity named Universal Salvation.
The Buddha told Shanming:

"These twelve deities have also made a vow before the Buddha that they shall protect those who uphold this Dharma and practice this *samyak-saṃbodhi-prabhāsa-samādhi-dharmaviniścaya-sthāna*, ensuring that there are five kinds of purity:
first, wherever the sutra is kept, the high seat must always be kept pure."
Second, burning incense and sweeping the ground to make it pure;
third, keeping one's clothing always clean;
fourth, keeping one's mind, speech, and intentions always pure.
"Fifth, when reading this sutra, one should first offer pure water to wash the hands and rinse the mouth, always maintaining purity;
this is the fifth.
Thereupon, the Buddha addressed Ānanda:
"I entrust to you this dharma of the Samādhi of Perfectly Accomplished Radiance; transcribe the scriptural text well and be careful not to add or subtract anything.
Diligently teach all people so that they may quickly receive and understand it."
Ānanda! This sutra is difficult to encounter. Why is this so?
Its prerequisite is to arise from the six perfections (ṣaṭ-pāramitā) before entering right concentration.

Within these one hundred and thirty-five practices, there are instructions on teaching, instructions on humility, instructions on patience, instructions on propriety, instructions on all wholesome dharmas, and instructions on the dharma of emptiness; indeed, up to the place of parinirvāṇa, there is nothing that is not fully contained therein.
All the marks and embellishments of the Buddha’s body, as well as his power of wisdom, all emerge from this Dharma.
It is the most honored and supreme, serving to sever birth and death; it is what is called the incomparable Dharma.
I entrust this to you once more; transmit it with careful attention so that it may be clearly understood.
The appearance of a Buddha in the world is difficult to encounter, and the arising of the Dharma’s exhortations is likewise rare to meet.
"Do not be negligent or distant.
Ānanda said, "I shall receive the instruction of the World-Honored One."

When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra, the enlightened ones and celestial deities who had come from the ten directions paid homage to the Buddha with joy and suddenly returned each to their own abodes.

The enlightened ones of the Land of Endurance, the assembly for the eradication of evil, the devas, nāgas, and ghost kings, as well as the fourfold assembly, were filled with delight upon hearing the sutra; they each touched their heads to the ground in prostration before the Buddha and departed.
The Sūtra on the Samādhi of Accomplished Radiance Spoken by the Buddha.
